recentItems.title: Why more AI data centers aren’t the answer | Dimitrios Nikolopoulos | TEDxMidAtlantic
recentItems.description:
We've been told the future of AI looks like ever-bigger data centers — warehouses that drink a town's water and draw a city's power so the same two chatbots can answer everyone's questions. Dimitrios Nikolopoulos, who has spent 30 years in high-performance computing, thinks that future is both unnecessary and a dead end. His provocation: the leaps in computing have almost never come from making machines bigger. They've come from making them smaller. An iPhone 7 outran the fastest supercomputer of 1995. A game console beats the one that topped the year 2000.

Follow that curve forward and the picture flips. Instead of intelligence locked inside a handful of remote, resource-hungry mega-centers, it could live on small, capable devices — the kind you could put in a home, a school, or a business. And that's not a downgrade; it's a more resilient, more private, more sustainable, and more personal way to compute, and it's exactly what his lab is building.

He brings it down to one example you can hold: a Socratic teaching assistant trained only on his course notes that never hands you an answer — it only asks better questions — running on a single small device that serves an entire classroom over Wi-Fi. The talk is a working researcher's argument that the most interesting frontier in AI isn't superintelligence in the cloud, but the supercomputer we could each have on the desk in front of us. Dimitrios Nikolopoulos is the John W. Hancock Professor of Engineering at Virginia Tech. He serves as a Professor in the Department of Computer Science while also holding a courtesy appointment in the Bradley Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. In these roles, he is dedicated to advancing knowledge and promoting discovery in High-Performance Computing and Computer Systems. His research efforts in these fields have had a significant impact on both academia and industry, aiding in the development of industry standards and the improvement of commercial software products.

Dimitrios’s scholarly contributions have been instrumental to the OpenMP parallel programming standard and have been adopted by RedHat Enterprise Linux and a variety of commercial system software products, including parallelizing compilers, in-memory databases, and data stream processing systems. His work has also catalyzed advancements in experimental operating systems and programming languages for multiprocessor systems. Further information about his scholarly work can be found in his profiles on DBLP, Google Scholar, ORCID, Scopus, and his CV. A short bio is also available, along with a Wikipedia entry about his work.

recentItems.title: What if Those Most Impacted by Displacement Designed the Future of Land | Ramla Sahid | TEDxSanDiego
recentItems.description:
What if the people most impacted by displacement got to design the future of land itself? Ramla Sahid shares how the Partnership for the Advancement of New Americans (PANA) purchased 2.2 acres of land to build Global Village, a community-owned project rooted in the belief that real belonging comes from ownership, not just having a voice — and that when communities own their own future, they create neighborhoods where children grow up knowing they belong.#Refugees #Belonging #HousingJustice #CommunityOwnership #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #TEDtalks #ImmigrantLed Ramla Sahid is the executive director of the Partnership for the Advancement of New Americans (PANA). Her work is shifting who holds power, who holds resources, and whose lives benefit from community investment. PANA ensures historically excluded communities have voice and influence over public investment, inclusive democracy, and policy priorities. She recently spearheaded the purchase of 2.2 acres of land for the Global Village: Refugee and Immigrant Cultural Hub and Housing Campus and oversaw a participatory visioning process with nearly 2,000+ community members to shape the programming, masterplan, and long-term community ownership of the site.

Sahid's experience guides her work. She is committed to leading efforts that produce changes in policies, practices, systems, organizational capacities, and community norms to improve health.

recentItems.title: Why Do Smart People Miss the Future? | Dev Patnaik | TEDxSanDiego
recentItems.description:
How is it that so many of us get blindsided by what’s coming next? Dev Patnaik explains how our wiring keeps our attention on the present, leaving us vulnerable to disruption and change. He shows how becoming more future focused can change the way we think, act and lead.
www.devpatnaik.com
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/devpatnaik/
#TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #TEDtalks #FutureFocused #Leadership #Disruption Dev Patnaik is the CEO of Jump Associates, the strategy firm for future focused leaders. Dev has been a trusted advisor to CEOs at some of the world’s most admired companies, including Starbucks, Target, Nike, Universal Music and Virgin. He’s a frequent keynote speaker at major forums, and his writing has appeared in BusinessWeek, Forbes, Fast Company, and many others. Dev is the author of Wired to Care, named one of the best books of the year by both Fast Company and Business Week. When not at Jump, Dev is an Adjunct Professor at Stanford University, where he teaches innovation methods to MBA and design students. Having witnessed the moments when bold bets were made and hard truths had to be faced, he has a rare perspective on what distinguishes leaders who shape the future from those who merely survive it. recentItems.title: Subtract to Succeed: The Case for Doing Less | Nell Derick Debevoise Dewey | TEDxSanDiego
recentItems.description:
You've been chasing gold stars and doing everything “right” since kindergarten. And you're exhausted. Nell Derick Debevoise Dewey argues the problem isn't your effort, your skills, or your ambition. It's that no one ever taught you what to subtract. After causing a car accident that could have been fatal, and finding the research on why our brains skip subtraction entirely, she offers a practical method to build success that feels as good as it looks. 

https://www.nell3d.com/
https://nell3d.substack.com/
#TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #TEDtalks
#SubtractToSucceed 
#RegenerativeLeadership 
#Burnout Nell Derick Debevoise Dewey is a Subtraction Activist, leadership strategist, and Forbes Senior Contributor who has spent her career helping ambitious, big-hearted high-achievers identify and build their own flavor of success. Nell's journey has crossed three sectors and four continents. She began in the not-for-profit sector, supporting youth activists globally and building mental health programs for refugee communities. She spent the next decade helping Fortune 500 executives, Ivy League MBAs, global NGO leaders, and government officials to align their skills, needs, and desired impact. Today, she leads her own B Corp, sharing the approach of Systematic Subtraction through content, tools, and coaching. Nell holds degrees from Harvard, Cambridge, Columbia, and London Business School, and is conscious she may have learned more about leadership from her horses than from any of those fine institutions. She writes the Substack, Subtract to Succeed, also the title of her forthcoming book. recentItems.title: Grit needs a grid | Louie Nguyen | TEDxSanDiego
recentItems.description:
There's a poverty we don't talk about. Forty percent of American kids are growing up with one caring adult in their lives — or none. Louie Nguyen, refugee-turned-nonprofit CEO, spent years believing grit explained his rise. He was wrong. This talk reveals what every child actually runs on — and the surprisingly small way anyone can become part of it.

recentItems.title: What surfing taught me about cancer | Tyler Callaway | TEDxSanDiego
recentItems.description:
Tyler texted this to Jami before the show - Jami still trying to clarify with Tyler 9-20-2026: What can surfing teach us about cancer?
Tyler Callaway is a lifelong surfer and multi-time cancer survivor whose colorful life has taken him from championship surfing and the surf industry to entrepreneurship, invention, philanthropy—and some experiences that sound almost impossible.
He was bitten by a shark in the morning, struck by lightning that same afternoon, and somehow walked away from both.
But those may not be the most important waves Tyler has faced.
After confronting cancer more than once, Tyler discovered that the lessons he learned in the ocean—humility, resilience, perspective, and empathy—could also help him navigate the biggest challenge of his life.  Seeing someone survive and thrive can help someone else fight to live. Paying it back by paying it forward. www.allwateradvantage.com #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #TEDtalks #Cancer #Surfing #giveback Tyler Callaway believes hope becomes real when people can see it in someone else. A four-time national surfing champion and East Coast Surfing Hall of Fame inductee, he spent decades in surfing before surviving cancer multiple times, an experience that reshaped his understanding of resilience and purpose. He co-founded the Legends Surfing Luau benefiting Moores Cancer Center, which has raised over $15 million for cancer research. Today, he is building a video-storytelling platform for cancer patients and survivors, helping them see that survival—and even thriving—is possible. He also connects biotech and research teams with the human impact of their work, bridging innovation and lived experience. Having survived cancer, a shark attack and a lightning strike, Tyler lives by one belief: seeing someone survive and thrive can change how you fight to live. “I’ve been incredibly lucky with early diagnoses and successful treatments. The least I can do is pay it back by paying it forward.” This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. recentItems.title: How maritime museums can save the ocean | Christina Connett Brophy, PhD | TEDxSanDiego
recentItems.description:
How can a museum save the ocean? Dr. Christina Connett Brophy, President and CEO of the Maritime Museum of San Diego, has an answer rooted in her own childhood at sea: by connecting people to the past, to each other, and to the future — one ship, one story at a time.

https://www.instagram.com/sdmaritime/
https://www.facebook.com/sdmaritime/

#TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #TEDtalks #BlueEconomy #OceanConservation
#MaritimeMuseum #SanDiegoMuseum Christina Connett Brophy, PhD, is President and CEO of the Maritime Museum of San Diego; an International Congress of Maritime Museums (ICMM) Executive Council member; Lead for the ICMM Maritime Refugees Project; Explorers Club Fellow; Board member of TMA BlueTech. She held leadership roles at Mystic Seaport Museum and the New Bedford Whaling Museum; taught at Rhode Island School of Design and is a member of the Advisory Committee of the Scripps Center for Marine Archaeology.

Connett Brophy has lectured in the United States, Canada, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East on maritime history, fine art, and cartography. She holds degrees from Northwestern University, University of Auckland, and University of Valencia.

A lifelong mariner, she grew up aboard the research vessel Geronimo, tagging sharks and turtles throughout the Atlantic for the National Marine Fisheries Service and the Archie Carr Foundation, an ongoing program founded by her parents and St. George’s School 50 years ago. recentItems.description:
Are You Living Joe Dreamz? #TEDxSanDiego #TEDx #TEDtalks #joedreamz #livejoedreamz #tedxsandiego 
JoeDreamz.com - people who are striving to live their dreams - @joedreamz Instagram My name is Joe Dreamz, born and raised in Slam Diego (Go Padres), California and I believe the world would be a better place if everyone was living their Dream! My stage name was inspired by Joseph, a character in the Bible who was famous for his ability to interpret dreams.

Now my dream is that someone can listen to a Joe Dreamz song, watch a D.R.E.A.M. podcast, wear the merch, or order a birthday freestyle and not have to wait until their car breaks down before they start living their dreams as well! recentItems.title: From food waste to food abundance | Prema Walker | TEDxRancho Mirage
recentItems.description:
Prema Walker, Founder and CEO of Prema’s Permaculture & Composting, outlines a durable model for local social entrepreneurship based on California's organic waste diversion law. She details how her proof-of-concept urban farm has successfully diverted over 700,000 pounds of organic waste from landfills to model micro-scale agricultural sustainability. Prema Walker is the Founder and CEO of Prema's Permaculture & Composting in the Coachella Valley. She grew up in India watching her grandfather farm land he had worked his entire life without ever building lasting financial security from it. When she settled in the Coachella Valley in 2020, she saw the same story among local growers, and it became one of the reasons she built her business.
She built that business on California's SB 1383, the state law mandating that organic waste be diverted from landfills. Recognizing that the mandate created a durable market, she has, since 2021, diverted more than 700,000 pounds of organic material from landfills, composting it and returning it to the communities that generated it. That work has secured roughly $275,000 in competitive funding while creating jobs, growing food, opening green spaces for communities,
and cutting the emissions that landfills release. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: What you're experiencing is not what's happening | Dr. Romi Ran | TEDxRancho Mirage
recentItems.description: Oxford-trained Clinical Psychologist Dr. Romi Ran discusses moving past traditional psychological frameworks to explore the core of human identity. Drawing from years of intensive contemplative practices, including extended solitary and darkroom retreats, she explains what it means to strip away societal identity and experience life more directly. Dr. Romi Ran is an Oxford-trained Clinical Psychologist, speaker, and author whose work explores the relationship between the mind, suffering, and human experience. After more than a decade working within traditional psychological frameworks, she became increasingly interested in the deeper mechanisms underlying thought, perception, and identity. Her perspective has been deeply shaped by several years of intensive contemplative practice, including extended solitary and dark room retreats, which continue to inform her clinical work. Her TEDx talk challenges the way we understand our own experience and explores what it means to experience life more directly. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Limits are learned, not biologically fixed | Ivan Borzenko | TEDxRancho Mirage
recentItems.description: Ultramarathon athlete Ivan Borzenko shares his journey from a childhood prognosis that he might spend his life in a wheelchair to completing a 320-mile triathlon and serving on an emergency medical team on Mt. Everest. His talk explores the invisible barriers society constructs around potential and challenges audiences to look beyond their perceived limits. Ivan was once told he may never walk and could spend his life in a wheelchair. Years later, he would go on to pursue a Guinness World Record during a 320-mile triathlon and serve with an emergency medical team on Mt. Everest. Through his story, Ivan explores the invisible barriers society builds around possibility and the ways those limits shape how people see themselves. Whether someone is facing challenges in their career, family, health, or personal goals, this is a reminder that our perceived limits are often much smaller than our true potential. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The garments of grief | Dr. Lynda Reid | TEDxRancho Mirage
recentItems.description: Following the passing of her husband, speaker and Professional Certified Coach Dr. Lynda Reid blends neuroscience, leadership research, and deeply personal experience to construct a transformative perspective on grief. She challenges the concept of "moving on" to explore how we actively carry loss as a continuing expression of love. Dr. Lynda Reid is a speaker, author, and Professional Certified Coach (PCC) whose work focuses on resilience, meaning, and human adaptation through life’s transitions. With a doctorate in education centered on multicultural leadership and growth through cultural immersion, she combines neuroscience, leadership research, and personal experience to help people navigate change, loss, and transformation. Following the death of her husband, Lynda developed a new perspective on grief that challenges the idea of “moving on” and instead explores how we learn to carry loss as a continuing expression of love. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
